![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252554/assets/ec9faab92da8de318d78e548adc35e8df20083816f8bafdacf0cfbbd497e084c.png)

The graphs of the functions $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ are given above. Find ${h}^{′}(-2)$ where $h(x)=f(x)g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
The product rule and the addition rule for derivatives give

$$
{h}^{′}(x)={f}^{′}(x)\cdot g(x)+f(x)\cdot {g}^{′}(x).
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(-2)={f}^{′}(-2)\cdot g(-2)+f(-2)\cdot {g}^{′}(-2).
$$

From the graphs above, we obtain that $f(-2)=0$ and $g(-2)=3.$

Additionally,

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (-4,0)$ equals $-1.$ So, ${f}^{′}(-2)=-1.$

- The slope of $g(x)$ on $x\in (-4,0)$ equals $\frac{1}{2}.$ So, ${g}^{′}(-2)=\frac{1}{2}.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(-2) & ={f}^{′}(-2)\cdot g(-2)+f(-2)\cdot {g}^{′}(-2)-{f}^{′}(-2) \\  & =-1\cdot 3+0\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$
